title: India–Russia

cards.b:
Russia (and the Soviet Union before it) has been India's most dependable great-power partner for 70 years. It supplied arms, vetoes at the UN and steel plants. Today the partnership is tested by the war in Ukraine, Russia's closeness to China and US pressure over oil.

UPSC asks how India balances this relationship with its growing ties to the US. The answer needs three things: the history, the four pillars (defence, energy, nuclear/space, diplomacy) and the 2022–26 stress points.

A neat line for your answer: India–Russia is a special and privileged strategic partnership (2010) built on trust, but today's trade is thin outside oil and arms.

cards.h: From the Soviet era to the present
cards.b:
The Soviets backed India on Kashmir at the UN, built the Bhilai steel plant and sold arms on easy rupee terms. The 1971 Treaty (Gromyko and Swaran Singh) gave India cover during the Bangladesh war. It contained a security clause (Article IX) short of an alliance.

After 1991 trade shrank, and the debt in rupees was settled by 'rupee-rouble' arrangements. The 2000 Declaration on Strategic Partnership restarted ties. Annual summits began in 2000, alternating between the two capitals.

Russia is still a leading arms supplier, but its share has fallen. SIPRI data show Russia's share of India's arms imports at about 36% in 2020–24, down from over 70% in 2010–14, as India diversified to France, the US and Israel and built more at home.

  • Platforms: Su-30MKI, T-90 tanks, INS Vikramaditya, Kilo submarines, the Kamov helicopters.
  • S-400 Triumf: bought in 2018 for about $5.4 billion despite the US CAATSA threat. Deliveries began in late 2021.
  • BrahMos: the joint venture (1998) that makes the supersonic cruise missile.
  • Co-production: AK-203 rifles at Amethi (Korwa), under Make in India.

Weak points: delays, spare-part shortages after sanctions, and cost overruns (the Admiral Gorshkov refit).

Nuclear: Rosatom builds the Kudankulam plant in Tamil Nadu. Units 1 and 2 operate and more are under construction. The 1988 agreement was signed before the NSG existed, and Russia backed India for NSG membership.

Oil: before 2022 Russia supplied under 2% of India's crude. After Western sanctions and the G7 price cap (December 2022, $60 a barrel), Russia sold at a discount. By 2023–24 Russia supplied about 35% of India's imports. India says it buys where it is cheapest to protect Indian consumers.

Space: Rakesh Sharma flew on Soyuz T-11 in 1984. Russia trained Gaganyaan astronaut candidates.

Connectivity: the INSTC (2000, with Iran), the Chennai–Vladivostok sea route and an Arctic/Northern Sea Route interest.

After the February 2022 invasion, India abstained on the UN resolutions and did not impose sanctions. It said it favoured dialogue and diplomacy and called for respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. Modi told Putin at Samarkand in September 2022 that today's era is not an era of war.

India also engaged Ukraine. Modi visited Kyiv in August 2024, the first Indian PM to do so. He had visited Moscow a month earlier for the annual summit.

India's critics abroad called it a 'free rider'. India's reply is the principle of strategic autonomy, and it points out that European states also kept buying Russian energy for months.

India hosted the G20 in 2023 and secured a New Delhi declaration that omitted direct condemnation of Russia, a diplomatic success for the Global South camp.

• August 2025: the US added 25% to its tariff on India for buying Russian oil (total 50%).
  • October 2025: US sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil. Reliance and other buyers sharply cut purchases from them.
  • July 2025: the EU sanctioned Nayara Energy (Rosneft owns about 49%).
  • 4–5 December 2025: Putin visited New Delhi for the 23rd annual summit. He promised 'uninterrupted' fuel supply. The sides signed a programme for economic cooperation to 2030, a labour mobility agreement and set a trade goal of $100 billion by 2030.
  • February 2026: the US announced it was dropping the 25% penalty after India said it would cut Russian oil. Trade data show a drop from the 2025 peak, but Russian crude still arrives; reports differ on volumes.

Bilateral trade was about $69 billion in FY2024-25, mostly Indian oil imports. India's exports to Russia are small, under $5 billion.

cards.h: Reliable friend or a fading partner?
cards.b:
Russia's 'no limits' partnership with China (February 2022) worries Delhi. Russia also sells arms to Pakistan in small quantities and recognised the Taliban government in July 2025.

Supporters argue Russia is a balancing power: India benefits from a multipolar world and a Russia not wholly dependent on China. Sceptics say India overestimates what Moscow can still do.

Commentators like C. Raja Mohan describe a 'managed decline' of the old partnership that India must carry without breaking.

• It diversifies arms: Rafale (France), P-8I, MQ-9B (US), Israeli systems.
  • It keeps Russia in useful forums: BRICS, SCO, the RIC idea (Russia–India–China).
  • It uses rupee and local-currency payments, plus UAE dirham, to avoid dollar exposure.
  • It invests in the Far East (a $1 billion line of credit in 2019).
  • It publicly separates 'Russia' from 'Ukraine war', saying it will support peace efforts.

The 2025–26 pressure shows the limits. India can adjust oil volumes but will not cut Russia off. In defence, S-400 and possible Su-57 offers show Russia still pitches high-end hardware.

Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership

The 2010 upgrade from the 2000 Strategic Partnership. Russia has this label only with India.

RELOS

A reciprocal logistics exchange agreement, signed in Moscow in February 2025, giving access to each other's facilities.

2+2

Foreign and defence ministers' dialogue. India–Russia held its first in 2021.

INSTC

A 7,200 km multimodal route linking Mumbai to Russia via Iran and the Caspian.

"India-Russia relations have stood the test of time. Examine in the context of the Ukraine war." (typical)
"Evaluate the role of defence cooperation in India–Russia relations." (typical)
"How has the changing global order affected India's Russia policy?" (typical)

Structure: (1) history: 1955, 1971, 2000, 2010; (2) pillars: defence, nuclear, energy, space, diplomacy; (3) Ukraine: abstentions, Samarkand, Kyiv; (4) 2025–26 pressure: tariffs, Rosneft/Lukoil sanctions, Dec 2025 summit; (5) assessment: strategic autonomy with limits; (6) way forward: diversify, deepen economic ties (INSTC, Far East), keep ties with Russia without losing the West.

quiz.q: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation was signed in:
quiz.w: It was signed in August 1971, before the Bangladesh war.

quiz.q: India elevated ties with Russia to a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership' in:
quiz.w: The 2000 label was 'Strategic Partnership'. The upgrade came in 2010.

quiz.q: The S-400 deal with Russia, signed in 2018, was valued at about:
Which US law threatened sanctions over India's S-400 purchase?
quiz.w: Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (2017).

quiz.q: Modi's remark 'This is not an era of war' was made at:
quiz.w: At the SCO summit in Samarkand, September 2022, in a meeting with Putin.

quiz.q: The first Indian PM to visit Kyiv was:
Which joint venture produces the BrahMos missile?
quiz.w: BrahMos Aerospace is a joint venture of DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (1998).

quiz.q: The nuclear power plant built with Russian help in Tamil Nadu is:
The US sanctioned which two Russian oil majors in October 2025?
quiz.w: The US Treasury sanctioned Rosneft and Lukoil on 22 October 2025.

quiz.q: INSTC links India to Russia through:
quiz.w: The International North-South Transport Corridor runs via Iran (Chabahar/Bandar Abbas) and the Caspian.
